flags.f3_filler_directive: TAGGING CONVENTION (structural, not a proof hint): helper lemmas you introduce while filling proofs must NOT carry a `-- @node:` tag. `@node` is reserved for plan/core node ids (`ass:`/`def:`/`lem:`/`thm:` prefixed); tagging a helper with its own Lean name breaks the F2 structural gate (P7: emitted tag with no plan entry). Leave every helper you create untagged.
flags.f2_scaffold_directive:
STRUCTURAL TAGGING (blocking F2 plan gate, code P7): every S-block declared in the plan's `env` array MUST be marked in the emitted Lean by its own `-- @env: <S-block id>` line, on its own line immediately above the declaration that most characteristically realizes that block's world. This is required for EVERY planned S-block, not only the first — a scaffold that tags one block and leaves the others untagged is refused by the gate. Where one S-block's world is realized across several files, tag the file carrying its defining object; a block may carry more than one `-- @env` tag if its world genuinely spans files. Keep the existing `-- @node: <id>` discipline unchanged: exactly one canonical primary declaration per delivered plan node.

CLASS NODES STAY STRUCTURES (blocking gate codes P2/P3). A core node that carries `by_member_properties` is a CLASS: keep its plan `lean_kind` as "structure" with `members` exactly equal to the core's `by_member_properties`, and put that node's single canonical `-- @node:` tag on the structure itself. When the core's `construction` ALSO describes companion objects (an estimator family, an induced risk, a derived functional), emit those as SEPARATE, UNTAGGED companion declarations in the same file. Never collapse a class node into a bundling `def`, never retag the node onto such a bundle, and never emit a bundle whose components are placeholders like `Set.univ` — a tuple of vacuous components is not a faithful rendering of a class. Do not rewrite a plan node's `lean_kind`/`members` away from the core during sync-back.

TAG NAMESPACE (blocking gate P7). A `-- @node:` tag may carry ONLY a plan/core node id (the `ass:` / `def:` / `lem:` / `thm:` prefixed identifiers in plan.json). NEVER tag a declaration with its own Lean name: helper and auxiliary lemmas you introduce while proving are companions and must stay UNTAGGED, however important they are. An `@node` tag whose value is a bare Lean identifier is rejected by the gate as an emitted tag with no plan entry. This applies to every declaration you add, including ones created mid-proof.

TAG VALUES ARE COPIED, NEVER INFERRED. The value after `-- @node:` must be character-for-character one of the node ids that literally appear as keys in plan.json. Never derive a tag from a declaration's name, name prefix, or subject matter — a lemma called `l1_foo` is about the l1 class, it is NOT a node called `l1`; a lemma called `blockEnergy_pos` is NOT a node called `blockEnergy_pos`. If a declaration has no corresponding plan.json key, it gets NO `@node` tag at all. An unlinkable tag fails the graph refresh even when it passes the plan gate.

proposed_from.topic: Exact degree dependence of the minimax MSE for total-treatment-effect estimation under beta-order neighborhood interference and unit-randomized Bernoulli design: prove the matched frontier R* asymp d*binom(d,k*)/n over the bounded-coefficient bounded-degree class, where k*(beta,p) is the exposed order max{k<=beta: (1-p)^k-(-p)^k != 0}, delivering both the least-favourable family and the attaining estimator, and showing that BOTH bounds of Cortez-Rodriguez, Eichhorn and Yu (JCI 2023, arXiv:2208.05553) are loose -- their d-free Theorem 2 lower bound by d^(k*+1) and their Theorem 1 d^(beta+2) variance bound by a factor d -- contrary to their printed diagnosis; verified block witness at beta=1, p=1/2 gives Theta(d^2/n) two-sidedly with no observation noise

proposed_from.literature_map: CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023, Introduction and Section 3, formulate the fixed-population TTE under known neighborhood interference and Bernoulli randomization.  Section 4 constructs SNIPE as a pseudoinverse or Riesz score; its centered score is the method adapted here.  Theorem 1 gives design unbiasedness and a coarse degree-polynomial variance bound.  Theorem 2 and its following discussion give a degree-free fuzzy-Le-Cam lower bound and explicitly call the degree gap an analytical weakness.  Section 5.3 and the conclusion document conservative variance estimation as a separate unresolved inference problem; this proposal does not claim to solve it.  HarshawSavjeWang2025 supplies the general design-based Riesz representation and is the source for treating SNIPE as a constrained Gram problem rather than inventing a new estimator.  YuAiroldiBorgsChayes2022 is the adjacent heterogeneous additive-interference model; it differs because the graph is unknown and historical baseline data are observed.  EichhornKhanUganderYu2026 extends pseudoinverse analysis to clustered designs and gives bounds, but no unit-Bernoulli minimax degree frontier.  WangLi2026 adds covariate adjustment and a less-conservative asymptotic variance estimator, but does not characterize exact degree-uniform SNIPE risk.  No retrieved paper states the exposed-order object \(k_\star\), the rate \(d\binom d{k_\star}/n\), or a degree-amplifying fuzzy block lower bound.  The closest published result is therefore CortezRodriguezEichhornYu2023; the exact gap is its \(d^{\beta+2}/n\)-type upper bound versus \(d\)-free lower bound.
